holidays.name: National Raspberry Cream Pie Day
holidays.description: A day to indulge in a creamy, tart-sweet pie piled high with fresh raspberries. Bakers and dessert lovers alike are encouraged to whip up or hunt down a slice of this pink-hued treat.
holidays.origin: Like many American food days, it appears to have been created through food-calendar listings and dessert enthusiasts rather than by any official proclamation, and its exact originator is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Raspberries are not true berries in the botanical sense. Each one is an aggregate fruit made up of dozens of tiny drupelets, each with its own seed.

holidays.name: Sea Serpent Day
holidays.description: A day for cryptid fans and ocean-monster believers to celebrate legendary sea creatures, from Nessie-style lake dwellers to colossal serpents lurking in the deep. Think maps with 'here be dragons' and a healthy dose of mystery.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance popular with cryptozoology fans and appears on various quirky holiday calendars. There is no single documented founder.
holidays.funFact: Sailors' reports of sea serpents may have been inspired by real animals like oarfish, which can grow over 30 feet long and are the longest bony fish in the world.

holidays.name: Particularly Preposterous Packaging Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day dedicated to packaging that is absurdly hard to open or ridiculously oversized. Think clamshell plastic that requires power tools and a tiny item rattling around in a giant box.
holidays.origin: It is a humorous unofficial observance that circulates on novelty holiday calendars. Its origin is generally credited to the shared frustration of consumers everywhere.
holidays.funFact: The infuriating hard plastic clamshell packaging is so common that 'wrap rage' is an actual term used to describe the frustration of trying to open it.

holidays.name: National Lighthouse Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate the towering beacons that have guided sailors safely home for centuries. Lighthouse enthusiasts celebrate by visiting a lighthouse, or admiring photos of one.
holidays.origin: The date marks the anniversary of August 7, 1789, when the U.S. Congress passed the Lighthouse Act, which put the federal government in charge of maintaining lighthouses. It was one of the first public works laws passed by the new government.
holidays.funFact: The Lighthouse Act of 1789 was signed by President George Washington, making lighthouses one of the first things the new federal government took responsibility for.

holidays.name: Purple Heart Day
holidays.description: A solemn day honoring the men and women who have been wounded or killed while serving in the U.S. military. Many communities hold ceremonies and thank recipients of the Purple Heart medal.
holidays.origin: It marks the anniversary of the day in 1782 when George Washington created the Badge of Military Merit, the precursor to the modern Purple Heart.
holidays.funFact: During World War II, so many Purple Hearts were manufactured in anticipation of invasion casualties that the surplus supply has still been issued to wounded service members in the decades since.
